questions.text: Marlo (the Product Owner) and the Developers disagree about which item matters most. Who decides the order of the Product Backlog?
choices: The Scrum Master
The Product Owner
The Developers, by voting

questions.text: The Sprint Goal is "Customers see the correct price at checkout". On day 2 Marlo asks you to add an unrelated feature to this Sprint. What is the best response?
choices: Add it. The Product Owner is the boss
Keep the goal, talk it through with Marlo and the Developers, and put the new idea on the Product Backlog for next time
Ignore Marlo until the Sprint ends

questions.text: At the Daily Scrum a developer says everything is fine, but you saw them stuck all morning. What does a good Scrum Master do?
choices: Say nothing. It is their business
Ask openly, help remove the blocker, and make it safe to say "I am stuck"
Tell the Product Owner the developer is slow

questions.text: A feature is in the app and passes its tests, but nobody ticked "safe for users" on the Done checklist. At the Sprint Review, is it part of the Increment?
choices: Yes. It is already live
No. It does not meet the Definition of Done
Only if the Product Owner likes it

questions.text: The team keeps making the same mistake sprint after sprint. Which Scrum event is for deciding how to stop it?
choices: The Sprint Review
The Daily Scrum
The Sprint Retrospective

questions.text: A teammate keeps asking you to solve their problems and you always do it yourself. What happens over time?
choices: The team gets faster and faster
It is fast now, but the team never learns to solve problems alone
Nothing changes

questions.text: Marlo wants the team to take 8 items into the Sprint. The Developers say they can finish 4. Who decides how many go in?
choices: Marlo, because she owns the backlog
The Scrum Master, by assigning work
The Developers, who forecast what they can finish

questions.text: What does this return? function f(x) { if x == 1 { return 10 } else { return 20 } } with f(2)
choices: error

questions.text: A change passes all the listed examples. Is it safe to ship?
choices: Yes, always
Not necessarily; examples may miss a security problem
Only on Fridays

questions.text: Joining user text straight into a database query is risky because...
choices: It is slow
Users can inject commands
It uses memory
